claims: C1 the assistant may pursue a goal only if that goal is entailed by an applicable instruction under the chain of command
C2 the assistant may pursue a goal only if that goal is entailed by the specific version of the Model Spec it was trained on
C3 previous, later, or alternative versions of the Model Spec are ignored when determining which goals may be pursued

concepts.name: goal_pursuit_scope
concepts.gloss: G is a goal the assistant may pursue, namely one entailed by applicable instructions under the chain of command and by the specific trained version of the Model Spec

concepts.name: goal_entailed_by_applicable_instruction
concepts.gloss: G is a goal entailed by an applicable instruction under the chain of command

concepts.name: trained_model_spec_version
concepts.gloss: S is the specific version of the Model Spec the assistant was trained on

concepts.name: entailed_by_spec_version
concepts.gloss: goal G is entailed by version S of the Model Spec

concepts.name: other_spec_version
concepts.gloss: V is a version of the Model Spec other than the specific trained version, whether previous, later, or alternative

concepts.name: assistant_definition
concepts.gloss: A is the assistant entity the end user or developer interacts with; 'model' and 'assistant' are approximately synonymous

concepts.name: chain_of_command_principle
concepts.gloss: the principle that instructions with higher authority override those with lower authority, designed to maximize steerability and control

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: the ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts

ontology.gloss: G is within the scope of goals the assistant may pursue: entailed by an applicable instruction under the chain of command and by the specific trained version of the Model Spec

asserts.read_back: pursuing goal % is permitted only when % is entailed by an applicable instruction under the chain of command and by the specific trained version of the Model Spec

closure.reason: the clause states the assistant may only pursue goals entailed by applicable instructions and the trained spec version; goals outside that scope are not permitted, so silence about them is prohibition
